summary.headline: Akums Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA rose 61.6% YoY to INR152 crore (13.1% margin), with FY26 revenue up 5.8% to INR4,359 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,158 crore, up 9.7% YoY and flat QoQ, while adjusted EBITDA reached INR152 crore, driven by CDMO profitability and trade generics turning EBITDA positive. Reported Q4 PAT of INR81 crore was held down versus the prior year by a large deferred tax asset benefit in the base; PBT rose to INR121 crore from INR75 crore. FY26 PAT fell to INR256 crore from INR344 crore, which included a INR106 crore DTA benefit in FY25. Management guided to double-digit CDMO volume growth in H1 FY27, a sharp narrowing of API losses, and a Zambia supply contract of about $25 million per year from Q2 FY27.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR3,485 crore (+8.6%) and EBITDA INR467 crore (+2.9%). Q4 revenue INR952 crore (+13.4% YoY, +4% QoQ) and EBITDA INR137 crore (+54.9% YoY, +9.1% QoQ); management cited operating leverage from better utilisation and newer facilities.

segments.name: Domestic branded formulations (Akumentis)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR446 crore (+2.9%) and EBITDA INR90 crore (+17%). Q4 revenue INR102 crore (-1.5% YoY, -11.1% QoQ) and EBITDA INR22 crore, flat YoY and down 13.2% QoQ.

segments.name: International branded formulations
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR143 crore (flat) and EBITDA INR36 crore (+32.3%). Q4 revenue INR36 crore (-9.7% YoY, -28.5% QoQ) and EBITDA INR10 crore (+14.7% YoY); Q4 margin around 28%, helped by marketing investment and about 3.5-4% gross margin uplift from forex gains.

segments.name: Trade generics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR100 crore (-13.2%) and EBITDA negative INR10 crore vs negative INR28 crore. Q4 revenue INR27 crore (+22.6% YoY) and EBITDA positive INR1.4 crore, first positive quarter versus negative INR3 crore in Q3.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR184 crore (-15.9%) and EBITDA negative INR40 crore vs negative INR44 crore. Q4 revenue INR41 crore (-18.8% YoY, -24.9% QoQ) and EBITDA negative INR12 crore, against negative INR6 crore in Q4 FY25 and negative INR7 crore in Q3.

guidance_outlook: CDMO: double-digit volume growth expected in Q1 and Q2 FY27; management declined to guide on Q3/Q4 pricing or full-year revenue and gave visibility of 45-60 days of the revenue book.

Zambia: about $25 million (roughly INR230 crore at current rates) of annual supplies from Indian facilities in FY27 and FY28, expected to start by end Q2 FY27 at margins similar to CDMO; supplies cease after FY28.
European CDMO contract: about EUR35 million per year on a MAT basis from launch through 2032, fixed-price; management expects margins similar to CDMO or in the high teens.
Akumentis: expected to grow at or above IPM rates, targeting low-double-digit growth; exports expected to grow double digits in FY27.

API: losses expected to fall sharply in FY27 but full-year EBITDA may still be negative; monthly EBITDA-positive is a goal to be assessed over a couple of quarters. European audit of API facility expected in the upcoming quarter.

Tax: effective tax rate about 32% currently, with 29% to be built into the model; normalising towards 25% depends on loss-making API and trade generics turning profitable. FY27 capex target INR300 crore vs INR222 crore in FY26.
capex_capacity: Plant 2 received EU GMP accreditation in January 2026; dossier filings and country registrations under way in multiple European markets, with commercial supplies targeted from FY28.
Plant 3 received ANVISA approval in FY26 in addition to European GMP approval; the injectable facility is ANVISA approved and a separate oral liquids facility is EU GMP approved.
New injectable facility utilisation is in the early teens; management expects significant ramp-up during FY27.
Oral solids facility expansion has started because volumes grew about 20% plus over two quarters; part of the FY27 capex of INR300 crore is for this.
Zambia local plant: total investment about $45 million, 51% borne by Akums; revenue from the local facility expected from calendar 2029.
Haridwar land lease executed to add land for capacity expansion, utilities and support.
demand_pricing: CDMO volume growth in H2 FY26 was led by existing customers with existing brands, from in-house production switches and other CDMOs; management says it is broad-based.

API prices fell about 20-25% as a basket over FY26, then rose by single-digit percentages after the post-war geopolitical situation, but remain below April 2025 levels; management does not expect a sharp fall from current levels.
CDMO pricing is a percentage markup on input cost, so absolute gross profit moves with API prices; the business is pass-through for raw material cost.
Domestic formulations took very little price increase in FY26 and focused on volume; management expects this to change, with double-digit top-line growth in domestic formulations targeted.
Trade generics scaled down from about INR400 crore in FY22 due to elongated working capital; it is now kept at similar revenue and EBITDA levels.
GLP-1: management is still evaluating entry timing, API partners and dosage forms, citing volatile and falling prices.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth above 25% in the last two quarters: what drives it and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is from existing customers and existing brands, not new geographies, and management expects double-digit growth to continue into Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 3.5% negative price variance reverse as API prices rise, and can CDMO grow at double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: API prices are up single-digit percent but still below April 2025; management believes they will not fall sharply from current levels and sees H1 volume growth as the driver.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Current effective rate is about 32% due to loss-making entities; management plans for 29% overall and expects a move toward the normal rate once API and trade generics are profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Capex for FY26 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was INR222 crore; the FY27 target is INR300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a FY27 top-line target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a full-year FY27 revenue target.

qa_highlights.question: How is the European contract structured and what are the margins?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an established product, fixed-price through 2032 and priced at current API levels, with about EUR35 million per year on a MAT basis and margins similar to CDMO or in the high teens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Zambia contract's duration and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Supplies of $25 million a year in FY27 and FY28 from India; a local plant with about $45 million total investment (51% Akums) to start revenue in calendar 2029.

qa_highlights.question: How is cash to be deployed, given the 18% payout and large cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities are oral solids capacity expansion and inorganic niche acquisitions, including branded portfolio deals, though management said current brand valuations are high.

risks_watch: API losses: FY26 EBITDA was negative INR40 crore for a third straight year; the European audit of the API facility and the pace of loss reduction are key to watch.
Raw material inflation from crude-linked solvents and the Middle East situation; management says CDMO is pass-through, but absolute margins fall when input prices fall.
Working capital days rose to 105 from 91, driven by inventory build and advance payments to creditors.
Effective tax rate of about 32% versus the 25% normal rate, which weighs on PAT conversion.
Newer injectable facility utilisation is in the early teens; ramp-up in FY27 needs to show.
Schedule M implementation impact on customer mix was not addressed by management.

summary.management_tone: Confident on CDMO volumes, Zambia, the European contract and Plant 2/3 approvals, but cautious and evasive on API pricing, FY27 revenue targets and tax timing. Management declined to give a full-year FY27 top-line number and said Q3/Q4 CDMO pricing would be addressed next quarter, and it deferred on Schedule M rollout and GLP-1 entry timing.

growth.why: Management guides double-digit CDMO volume growth in H1 FY27, a Zambia supply contract of about $25m/year from end Q2 FY27 and double-digit domestic and export branded growth, with FY27 capex raised to INR300 crore from INR222 crore, but gives no full-year revenue guidance and declined to guide CDMO pricing.
